answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks via superlinear stake burning. To register or validate transactions, each node burns cryptographic stake scaled quadratically by the network node index, $C_n = k \cdot n^2$. A single attacker deploying $M$ fake identities must absorb costs scaling superlinearly as $O(M^3)$, turning any prospective profit into an economic zephyr that dissipates instantly. One malicious ripple in the pool triggers exponential penalty escalations, driving the adversary over a solvency ledge into catastrophic capital exhaustion.
